How Kubernetes, helm and these images behave: A StatefulSet with updateStrategy RollingUpdate replaces its pods one at a time from the highest ordinal, deleting each old pod before it creates its replacement (there is no surge); with partition N, pods with an ordinal below N keep the old version; with OnDelete no pod is replaced until someone deletes it. A replacement pod mounts the same PVCs from volumeClaimTemplates. A pod's emptyDir volumes and its container filesystem are deleted together with the pod; only data on a PersistentVolume outlives it. When a PVC is deleted, its PersistentVolume and the data on it are deleted if the reclaimPolicy is Delete; with Retain the volume and its directory stay on the node (Released). Deleting a StatefulSet or scaling it down keeps the PVCs created from its volumeClaimTemplates, unless its persistentVolumeClaimRetentionPolicy says Delete for that case (whenDeleted or whenScaled). A StatefulSet pod that is deleted is recreated with the same name and the same PVC name; if that PVC is gone, a new empty one is created. The postgres image applies POSTGRES_PASSWORD and POSTGRES_HOST_AUTH_METHOD only when it initializes an empty data directory; a data directory that already holds a database keeps its users, passwords and pg_hba.conf. An empty data directory is initialized as a new, empty database. A Service sends connections only to ready pods whose labels match every key of its selector, on its targetPort (a number, or the name of a container port of those pods); with no such pod, or nothing listening there, connections fail. A pod whose image cannot be pulled never starts (ImagePullBackOff); a pod whose memory limit is below what its process needs is killed (OOMKilled) and restarted again and again.

The questions are about the state after all these actions.
